firstAid.title: Cattle First Aid Protocols
firstAid.subtitle: Essential step-by-step emergency care instructions before the veterinarian arrives.
firstAid.isolationDesc: Separate the sick animal immediately to a shaded, dry, well-ventilated space.
firstAid.hydrationDesc: Provide clean lukewarm water with salt/jaggery. Offer soft green gruel.
firstAid.lesionsDesc: Wash mouth and foot sores gently with 1% Potassium Permanganate or Neem water.
firstAid.tempDesc: Check rectal temperature using a digital thermometer twice daily.
firstAid.bloatDesc: Keep front legs elevated on a slope. Drench 500ml vegetable oil mixed with turpentine.
firstAid.udderDesc: Milk out affected teats completely every 3 hours and discard milk safely.
firstAid.doNotDoTitle: Critical Warnings - What NOT to Do
firstAid.warning1: NEVER force liquids down the throat if the animal is lying flat or unconscious.
firstAid.warning2: NEVER cut or puncture swollen muscle lumps in suspected Black Quarter.
firstAid.warning3: NEVER use dirty unsterilized needles or knives on wounds.

vaccines.title: Vaccination Schedule & Calculator
vaccines.subtitle: Keep your cattle protected against deadly contagious outbreaks with timely immunizations.
vaccines.calcDesc: Enter your calf's age in months to calculate due dates for FMD, HS, BQ, Anthrax, and Brucellosis vaccines.
vaccines.vetDisclaimerBody: Vaccines must be administered under the supervision of a certified veterinarian. Maintain strict 2°C to 8°C cold chain storage.
vaccines.note1: Deworm cattle 2 weeks prior to vaccination for maximum immunity response.
vaccines.note2: Never vaccinate sick, severely malnourished, or heavily stressed animals.
vaccines.note3: Do not vaccinate cows in advanced pregnancy (last 30 days) unless instructed by a vet.

emergency.whatToDoTitle: What To Do During an Emergency
emergency.whatToDoSubtitle: Follow these essential steps immediately when your animal shows signs of critical illness or injury.
emergency.warningSignsSubtitle: Recognize critical symptoms requiring immediate emergency veterinary attention.

warnings.notStandingDesc: Inability to rise due to severe weakness, paralysis, or milk fever.
warnings.bleedingDesc: Uncontrolled bleeding from trauma, severe injuries, or internal hemorrhage.
warnings.breathingDesc: Gasping, open-mouth breathing, tongue protruding, or extreme panting.
warnings.feverDesc: Body temperature exceeding 104°F with severe shivering and body heat.
warnings.bloatingDesc: Rapid swelling on the left flank threatening organ compression.
warnings.seizuresDesc: Uncontrolled muscle twitching, convulsions, or loss of consciousness.
warnings.snakeBiteDesc: Sudden swelling on nostrils or limbs, drooling, and sudden collapse.
warnings.poisoningDesc: Sudden foaming, severe diarrhea, vomiting, or ingestion of toxic weeds/chemicals.
